meta.title: Timeline of Middle-earth history
meta.description: An overview of Middle-earth’s history milestones: Second Age, Third Age and a detailed view of the War of the Ring 3019. Three levels of detail for newcomers and fans.

description: An overview of Middle-earth’s history milestones: Second Age, Third Age and a detailed view of the War of the Ring 3019. Three levels of detail for newcomers and fans.
title: Timeline of history
subtitle: Three levels of detail — from ten milestones for newcomers to a detailed view of the War of the Ring.
intro: Tolkien’s chronicle of the history of Middle-earth is recorded in ages. The Second Age ended with Sauron’s fall at the gates of Mordor and the rise of the Shadow that would, in the Third Age, lead to open war. To help you orient yourself, we offer three levels of detail — pick what you need.
abbrev_post_pre: . Years are given according to Tolkien’s appendices; in some cases we round. The Lord of the Rings event takes place in our
abbrev_post_post: close to the Third Age — the exact setting differs from year to year.

paragraphs: For the oldest events no simple modern calendar can be used. The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so for the mythic beginning and the First Age we give no dates at all and keep to the order of events instead.

Tolkien also changed some details during his lifetime. Where differing versions exist, we prefer a note to false precision — we would rather write „about“ and explain why than pick one number and pretend there is no doubt about it.

**We always keep the game conception of The Lord of the Rings separate from Tolkien's chronology.** Everything up to the Fourth Age comes from the books. Our own decisions for the larp are in a separate block at the end of the page, marked with a label.
how_to_read.canon_intro: Events without a label follow the Tale of Years (Appendix B of The Lord of the Rings) or another of Tolkien's texts. A label is a warning that the date needs to be handled with care.

primary.label: Attested
primary.desc: The date is given by the Tale of Years or by another of Tolkien's texts. We do not mark such events with a label.

derived.label: Inferred
derived.desc: We infer the date or the connection from several places in the text; they are not recorded this way in any single chronicle.

uncertain.label: Approximate date
uncertain.desc: The Tale of Years gives the year as approximate („about“) or only as a period.

conflicting_versions.label: Several versions
conflicting_versions.desc: Tolkien left differing datings or wordings for the event. We give a note instead of a single number.

game_interpretation.label: PP game conception
game_interpretation.desc: Our decision for the larp, not Tolkien's canon.

labels.expand_hint: Tap to expand the detailed timeline.

quick_p: Ten milestones that are enough to orient you in the story of The Lord of the Rings.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The Great Music and the making of Eä
events.summary: Eru Ilúvatar creates the Ainur and through their Music the design of the world comes into being. Melkor brings his own discord into the Music and becomes the first great adversary. Sauron is later his servant, not the origin of evil.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The shaping of Arda
events.summary: The Valar and the Maiar enter the world to prepare it for the Children of Ilúvatar. Melkor destroys and mars their work again and again, so the shape of Arda changes several times.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The awakening of the Elves
events.summary: The Elves awaken as the Firstborn. Some accept the invitation of the Valar to the West, others remain in Middle-earth — and with that begins the great division of the Elven peoples, which lasts until the end of the Third Age.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The return of the Noldor and the wars against Morgoth
events.summary: Morgoth steals the Silmarils and flees to Middle-earth. Fëanor and a great part of the Noldor follow him and found great Elven kingdoms in Beleriand, which wage long wars against Morgoth.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The coming of Men
events.summary: With the first rising of the Sun, Men come into the world. The three houses of the Edain ally themselves with the Elves against Morgoth, and their descendants are later given Númenor.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: Beren and Lúthien
events.summary: A mortal Man and an Elven princess win one Silmaril from Morgoth's crown. From their line later come Elrond, Elros, the kings of Númenor and Aragorn.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The fall of the great realms
events.summary: Morgoth gradually destroys Nargothrond, Doriath, Gondolin and the other centres of resistance. The Elven kingdoms of Beleriand fall apart and the survivors withdraw to the havens by the sea.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: Eärendil and the War of Wrath
events.summary: Eärendil sails to the West and asks the Valar for help. Morgoth is defeated and cast out of the world, but most of Beleriand sinks beneath the sea. Sauron escapes judgement and stays behind in Middle-earth.

events.title: The founding of Númenor
events.summary: The Edain are given an island kingdom as a reward for their fight against Morgoth. Elros becomes its first king and his descendants rule Númenor for more than three thousand years.

events.title: The founding of Eregion
events.summary: Noldorin craftsmen found a land at the West-gate of Khazad-dûm and build unusually close ties with the dwarves. Nowhere else was the friendship of Elves and Dwarves so near.

events.title: Annatar and the Rings of Power
events.summary: Sauron comes in fair form as Annatar. He helps the Elven smiths make part of the Rings of Power and secretly forges the One Ring, with which he means to rule their bearers.

events.title: The War of the Elves and Sauron
events.summary: Eregion is destroyed, Celebrimbor falls and Elrond founds Rivendell as a refuge. Númenórean help finally defeats Sauron's armies and drives them east.

events.title: Sauron taken to Númenor
events.summary: King Ar-Pharazôn carries Sauron off as a captive. Sauron, however, becomes his counsellor and hastens the fall of the kingdom, whose decline had begun long before he arrived.

events.title: The fall of Númenor
events.summary: Númenor is destroyed after the king's assault on Aman. Elendil, Isildur, Anárion and the Faithful escape to Middle-earth in nine ships.

events.title: The founding of Arnor and Gondor
events.summary: The Faithful found two Realms in Exile with a common Númenórean origin. That is why Arnor and Gondor share the same laws, the same line of kings and the same inheritance of the palantíri.

events.title: The Last Alliance
events.summary: Elves and Men march out against Sauron together. Sauron is defeated before Barad-dûr, but Isildur keeps the One Ring instead of destroying it.

events.title: The Disaster of the Gladden Fields
events.summary: Isildur and his escort are ambushed by orcs and he is slain. The One Ring betrays him and stays lost in the Anduin for two and a half thousand years.

events.title: The division of Arnor
events.summary: After the death of King Eärendur the North-kingdom breaks up into Arthedain, Cardolan and Rhudaur. Arnor did not fall in a single blow — first it divided, and only a thousand years later did it perish entirely.

events.date_note: The exact time of the coming of the Istari is not consistent across Tolkien's texts.
events.title: The coming of the Istari
events.summary: Wizards come to Middle-earth to support the resistance against Sauron — not to rule over Men. Saruman later turns that task to his own advantage.

events.title: Angmar and the fall of the northern kingdoms
events.summary: The Witch-king breaks down the successor states of Arnor. Arthedain falls in 1974 and Angmar is defeated shortly afterwards — but the North-kingdom is never restored.

events.title: The fall of Khazad-dûm
events.summary: While digging for mithril the dwarves wake a Balrog deep beneath the mountains. Durin VI and Náin I both fall and Khazad-dûm is abandoned; from that time it is called Moria.

events.title: The fall of Minas Ithil
events.summary: The Nazgûl take Gondor's eastern fortress, and it becomes Minas Morgul. The palantír of the city falls into Sauron's hands.

events.title: The end of the royal line of Gondor
events.summary: King Eärnur accepts the Witch-king's challenge and never returns from Minas Morgul. From then on Gondor is governed by the Ruling Stewards — which is why it has no king at the end of the Third Age.

events.title: The One Ring is found
events.summary: Déagol finds the Ring in the Anduin and Sméagol murders him for it. Over the following hundreds of years Sméagol turns into Gollum.

events.title: The founding of Rohan
events.summary: Eorl the Young comes to Gondor's aid on the Field of Celebrant. Steward Cirion grants Calenardhon to Eorl's people and Rohan comes into being — on land that the Dunlendings regarded as their own.

events.title: Helm's war
events.summary: Wulf and the Dunlendings seize Edoras. Helm Hammerhand holds out in the fortress that has borne the name Helm's Deep ever since. This conflict explains the lasting hatred between the Dunlendings and the Rohirrim.

events.title: Smaug takes Erebor
events.summary: The dragon drives Durin's Folk out of the Lonely Mountain and destroys the town of Dale. The North loses its richest kingdom and the dwarven houses are scattered.

events.title: The War of the Dwarves and the Orcs
events.summary: The dwarven houses wage a war of vengeance after the death of King Thrór. The conflict culminates in the battle of Azanulbizar before the East-gate of Moria.

events.title: The quest of Erebor
events.summary: Smaug falls, Dale and Erebor are restored and the Battle of Five Armies is fought. On that journey Bilbo finds the One Ring and the White Council drives Sauron out of Dol Guldur.

events.title: Sauron returns openly
events.summary: Sauron declares his presence in Mordor and Barad-dûr is raised again. From that time on Gondor prepares for a great war.

events.title: Bilbo's 111th birthday
events.summary: Bilbo leaves the Shire and passes the Ring on to Frodo. Gandalf begins to suspect which ring it is.

events.title: The War of the Ring
events.summary: The One Ring leaves the Shire, the Fellowship is formed, Rohan and Gondor face assault, and on 25 March 3019 the Ring is destroyed in Orodruin. At the same time there is fighting in Lórien, in Mirkwood and at Erebor.

events.date_note: The Gondorian and the Hobbit reckoning date the beginning of the Fourth Age differently — see the note below.
events.title: The end of the Third Age
events.summary: The Ring-bearers sail from the Grey Havens. The age of the rule of Men begins.

ages_section.intro: A more detailed chronology for those who are building a character or want to know exactly what their people were doing two thousand years ago. Every age is collapsed — open only the one you need right now.

third_p: Selected milestones of the Third Age — the fall of the Northern Kingdom, the rise of Rohan, the return of the Shadow and the start of the War of the Ring.

ages.h2: The mythic beginning and the Years of the Trees
ages.intro: This part is not meant to compete with an encyclopaedia of The Silmarillion. It is here to explain the roots of the peoples and conflicts that surface in the Second and Third Ages — why the Elves are divided, where the Dwarves came from and whose servant Sauron originally was.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The Great Music of the Ainur
events.summary: Eru sets the themes of the Music before the Ainur. Melkor tries to press his own will, but even his discord cannot undo Ilúvatar's design — it can only bend it.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: Eä and Arda
events.summary: Ilúvatar gives the Music a real existence. Part of the Ainur enter Eä and work at the shaping of Arda; the greatest of them are later known as the Valar, the rest as the Maiar. To this second group belong both Sauron and the wizards.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The Lamps and the first wars
events.summary: The Valar build a first ordered world, lit by two great lamps. Melkor destroys their work, the lamps fall and the shape of Arda changes; the Valar withdraw westward into Aman.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The Two Trees of Valinor
events.summary: Yavanna makes Telperion and Laurelin, whose light gives Valinor its day and night. That light is later preserved in the Silmarils cut by Fëanor.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The awakening of the Elves
events.summary: The Elves awake beside the lake of Cuiviénen. The decision whether or not to set out for the West founds the main Elven divisions — the Noldor, the Sindar, the Silvan Elves and the Avari all have their origin in that choice.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The making of the Dwarves
events.summary: Aulë makes the Seven Fathers of the Dwarves out of a longing for pupils of his own. Ilúvatar accepts his work, but the Dwarves are to awake only after the Elves. From this come the dwarven temper and their peculiar place in the world.

events.year: End of the Years of the Trees
events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The destruction of the Two Trees
events.summary: Melkor and Ungoliant destroy the Trees, Melkor slays King Finwë and steals the Silmarils. Fëanor swears his Oath and leads the Noldor to Middle-earth — with consequences that weigh on the Elves throughout the First Age.

ages.intro: The First Age explains the origin of the Edain, the line of Beren and Lúthien and the ruin of Beleriand. We give no dates here — Tolkien's dating of the First Age differs between versions and the conversion of the Years of the Trees into solar years is disputed.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The first rising of the Sun and the awakening of Men
events.summary: With the rising of the Sun and the Moon the counting of solar years begins. Men come into the world at the time of the return of the Noldor; some houses journey west into Beleriand and become the Edain.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The Elven kingdoms of Beleriand
events.summary: Doriath, Gondolin, Nargothrond and other realms arise. Their people are not one nation — the Noldor, the Sindar and the Silvan Elves have different origins and their mutual relations are often strained.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: Beren and Lúthien
events.summary: Their line joins the fates of Elves, Men and Maiar. This genealogy is the key to Elrond, Elros and Aragorn — it is the ground of the Dúnedain's claim to the kingship.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: The great defeats
events.summary: Dagor Bragollach and the Nirnaeth Arnoediad break the power of Morgoth's opponents. Then follow the fall of Nargothrond, of Doriath and of Gondolin; the survivors hide at the Mouths of Sirion.

events.date_note: The Years of the Trees cannot be reliably converted into solar years, so we give no date.
events.title: Eärendil's voyage and the War of Wrath
events.summary: Eärendil sails to the West and the hosts of the Valar defeat Morgoth. Beleriand for the most part sinks and Morgoth is cast out of the world — but Sauron escapes judgement and stays in Middle-earth as the heir of his work.

ages.intro: The Second Age matters most for understanding the end of the Third: it explains Númenor and its fall, the making of the Rings of Power, the common origin of Arnor and Gondor, and why Sauron was able to keep returning.

events.title: The Grey Havens and Lindon
events.summary: Círdan founds Mithlond at the mouth of the Lhûn. Gil-galad rules Lindon, the chief Elven land of western Middle-earth and the direct heir of the kingdoms of Beleriand.

events.title: Elros, first King of Númenor
events.summary: Elros, Elrond's brother, chooses the fate of Men. His descendants rule Númenor and their line carries both long life and the royal claim to which Aragorn still appeals.

events.title: The first great Númenórean voyages
events.summary: The Númenóreans renew contact with the Men and Elves of the coasts of Middle-earth. Over the following centuries, however, some of them turn from benefactors and teachers into colonisers and overlords — and from here the road leads to Umbar and to the Black Númenóreans.

events.title: Eregion
events.summary: Celebrimbor and the Gwaith-i-Mírdain build a land of craftsmen at the West-gate of Khazad-dûm. Here the friendship of Elves and Dwarves reaches a closeness never repeated anywhere else.

events.title: Sauron as Annatar
events.summary: In fair form Sauron tries to win the trust of the Elven lords. Gil-galad and Elrond refuse him, but in Eregion he is received as a teacher — for he offers exactly what the craftsmen long for.

events.date_note: Tolkien returned more than once to the dating of the forging of the rings; the Tale of Years gives the years as approximate.
events.title: The making of the Great Rings
events.summary: With Annatar's help the Elven smiths make sixteen Great Rings. The three mightiest are finished later by Celebrimbor alone, without Sauron's direct part — which is why they are not directly corrupted by the One Ring.

events.title: The One Ring
events.summary: Sauron forges the One Ring in Orodruin and completes Barad-dûr. The Elves perceive his purpose and cease to use the Three for as long as Sauron holds the Ring.

events.title: The War of the Elves and Sauron
events.summary: Sauron destroys Eregion, kills Celebrimbor and seizes part of the Rings of Power. Elrond founds Rivendell as a stronghold of resistance. In the end a Númenórean army defeats Sauron and drives him out of Eriador.

events.date_note: The Tale of Years gives an approximate date; elsewhere Tolkien dates the first appearance of the wraiths differently.
events.title: The first appearance of the Nazgûl
events.summary: The bearers of the Nine Rings fall wholly under Sauron and appear as Ringwraiths. They are neither ghosts nor the dead — they are men whose own will the rings have taken away.

events.title: The division of Númenor
events.summary: In Númenor the fear of death and the resentment of the Ban of the Valar grow. Society splits into the King's Men and the Faithful. This decline begins long before Sauron's arrival — Sauron merely used it and brought it to its end.

events.title: Ar-Pharazôn brings Sauron in
events.summary: The king brings Sauron to Númenor as a captive. Sauron becomes his counsellor, turns most of the court to the worship of the Darkness and persuades the king that immortality can be won by attacking Aman.

events.title: Akallabêth — the Downfall of Númenor
events.summary: Númenor is drowned after the assault on Aman and the world is changed. Sauron loses the ability to take a fair form; the Faithful escape eastward in nine ships.

events.title: The Realms in Exile
events.summary: Elendil founds Arnor, his sons Isildur and Anárion found Gondor. They bring with them the palantíri, scions of the White Tree and Númenórean learning — an inheritance the two realms share.

events.title: Sauron attacks Gondor
events.summary: Minas Ithil falls. Isildur flees north up the Anduin to his father, while Anárion defends Osgiliath and Gondor.

events.title: The Last Alliance
events.summary: Gil-galad and Elendil gather the hosts of Elves and Men. After the battle on Dagorlad follows a seven-year siege of Barad-dûr. Gil-galad, Elendil and Anárion fall, Sauron is defeated — and Isildur keeps the Ring.

ages.intro: Three thousand years in which the North-kingdom perishes, Rohan is born, Moria is emptied, Erebor falls and the Shadow returns twice. Most of the ruins the characters pass at the end of the age are dated right here.

events.title: The Gladden Fields
events.summary: Isildur's escort is ambushed by orcs on the road north. The Ring betrays its holder and remains lost in the Anduin; three of his sons fall with Isildur and the North-kingdom loses most of its Dúnadan nobility.

events.title: Arnor divided
events.summary: After the death of King Eärendur his heirs divide the North-kingdom into Arthedain, Cardolan and Rhudaur. The quarrel over the fortress of Amon Sûl and its palantír weakens the northern states for a long time to come.

events.date_note: The dating of the coming of the Istari varies across Tolkien's texts.
events.title: Istari
events.summary: Wizards come to Middle-earth as messengers of the Valar. Saruman is at first the head of their order; Gandalf receives the ring Narya from Círdan.

events.title: The Shadow in Greenwood
events.summary: In the south of the great forest the fortress of Dol Guldur is raised. The wood gradually comes to be known as Mirkwood, and Sauron hides in it under the name of the Necromancer, with no one guessing who he is.

events.title: Angmar
events.summary: In the north Angmar arises, led by the Witch-king, the first of the Nazgûl. Rhudaur passes under his influence, and from then on the hobbits and the Dúnedain of the north live in the shadow of war.

events.title: The great assault of Angmar
events.summary: Cardolan is laid waste and Arthedain gravely weakened. Amon Sûl is destroyed, the defenders hold on around Fornost, and the dead of the Barrow-downs earn their evil name.

events.title: The founding of the Shire
events.summary: Marcho and Blanco receive land beyond the Brandywine from the king of Arthedain. The hobbits acknowledge the northern king but govern the country themselves — and after the fall of Arthedain that self-rule simply stays with them.

events.title: The Great Plague
events.summary: The plague comes out of the east and ravages Gondor, Eriador and other lands. Osgiliath loses a great part of its people, the watch on the borders of Mordor falls apart and the northern kingdoms grow weaker still.

events.title: The Wainrider wars
events.summary: A confederation of Easterlings threatens Gondor for almost a hundred years. King Ondoher falls in battle and the crisis of succession opens the way for the captain Eärnil II.

events.title: The fall of Arthedain and the defeat of Angmar
events.summary: Angmar takes Fornost, King Arvedui flees to the northern coast and dies there. The hosts of Gondor, Lindon and the northern allies then crush Angmar on the Green Fields — but Arnor is never restored and the Dúnedain become Rangers.

events.title: Durin's Bane
events.summary: While digging for mithril the dwarves wake a Balrog in the depths of Moria. Durin VI and his son Náin I both fall, Khazad-dûm is abandoned and Durin's Folk scatter to the Grey Mountains and the Blue Mountains.

events.title: Minas Ithil
events.summary: The Nazgûl besiege the city for two years and at last take it. The fortress becomes Minas Morgul and its palantír falls into Sauron's hands. With it Gondor loses the eastern gate of its own land.

events.title: Eärnur disappears
events.summary: The last king of Gondor accepts the Witch-king's challenge, rides into Minas Morgul and does not return. With no heir left, the rule of the Stewards begins, and they keep the throne empty „until the king returns“.

events.title: The Watchful Peace
events.summary: Sauron leaves Dol Guldur for the east and for almost four centuries there is relative quiet in Eriador and in Gondor. In just this period both sides get to draw breath — and then Sauron comes back stronger.

events.title: Sauron and the Ring
events.summary: Sauron returns to Dol Guldur and the White Council meets for the first time. At the same time Déagol finds the Ring in the Anduin and Sméagol takes it from him by murder.

events.title: The Uruk assault on Ithilien
events.summary: A new generation of stronger orcs out of Mordor takes Osgiliath and destroys its great bridge. Gondor is pushed off the eastern bank of the Anduin for good.

events.title: The Field of Celebrant
events.summary: Eorl the Young rides down from the north and saves the army of Gondor from the Balchoth and the orcs. Steward Cirion and Eorl swear their oath, Calenardhon becomes Rohan — and the Dunlendings who pastured there are driven out.

events.title: Helm's war and the Long Winter
events.summary: Wulf and the Dunlendings, helped by the corsairs, seize Edoras. Helm Hammerhand holds out in the fortress of the Hornburg, which has been called Helm's Deep ever since. After a cruel winter Fréaláf restores the kingdom and Saruman is given the keys of Orthanc.

events.title: The fall of Erebor
events.summary: Smaug the Golden destroys the town of Dale and seizes the Lonely Mountain. Thrór, Thráin II and Thorin escape; the North loses its richest kingdom and the trade axis of the Long Lake.

events.title: Thrór and the War of the Dwarves and the Orcs
events.summary: Azog kills Thrór at the East-gate of Moria. For nine years the dwarven houses wage a war of vengeance which culminates in the terrible battle of Azanulbizar — they win it, but they do not enter Moria.

events.title: Gandalf in Dol Guldur
events.summary: Gandalf makes his way into Dol Guldur and confirms that the Necromancer is Sauron. There he finds the dying Thráin II and receives the key and the map to Erebor.

events.title: The events of The Hobbit
events.summary: Thorin's company reaches Erebor, Smaug falls and the Battle of Five Armies decides the fate of the north-east. At the same time the White Council drives Sauron out of Dol Guldur — but he only goes where he had long meant to go.

events.title: The return to Mordor
events.summary: Sauron returns to Mordor and in 2951 declares himself openly. Barad-dûr is raised again, the Nazgûl reoccupy Dol Guldur and Gondor begins to live in preparation for war.

events.title: Saruman secures Isengard
events.summary: Saruman begins to act as an independent lord of Orthanc, fortifies it and builds forces of his own. It is not simply that he has yielded to Sauron — he wants power of his own, and in the end the One Ring for himself.

events.title: Balin's expedition
events.summary: Balin tries to refound Moria and for a few years he succeeds. The colony is then destroyed by orcs and other enemies out of the deeps of the mountains; the Fellowship finds its record twenty-five years later.

events.title: Bilbo's 111th birthday
events.summary: Bilbo leaves the Shire and, at Gandalf's insistence, leaves the Ring behind for Frodo. Gandalf begins to search the archives of Gondor for Isildur's record.

events.title: Gollum in Mordor
events.summary: Gollum is captured and questioned by Sauron. The names „Shire“ and „Baggins“ set the Nazgûl on the trail of the Ring — from that moment Frodo's departure is a matter of months.

wotr_p: A detailed breakdown of the two years in which the main story of The Lord of the Rings takes place. Dates are given according to the Gondorian calendar.

years.label: The year 3018
years.intro: The year in which everything is decided before anyone marches out to battle.

events.title: Gandalf reveals the truth about the Ring
events.summary: Gandalf tells Frodo that Bilbo's ring is the One Ring. Frodo decides to leave the Shire, but prepares his departure so as not to attract attention — half a year passes between the decision and the leaving.

events.title: The attack on Osgiliath and on Thranduil's realm
events.summary: Sauron's forces assail the fords at Osgiliath and at the same time the Woodland Realm in Mirkwood. It is during the northern attack that Gollum escapes from captivity. After the battle at the fords Boromir sets out to seek counsel in Rivendell.

events.title: Gandalf imprisoned on Orthanc
events.summary: Gandalf comes to Isengard for counsel. Saruman reveals his purpose to him — he wants the Ring for himself, not for Sauron — and imprisons him on the pinnacle of Orthanc.

events.title: The escape from Orthanc
events.summary: Gandalf escapes on the eagle Gwaihir and later, in Rohan, wins Shadowfax.

events.title: The Nazgûl in Eriador
events.summary: The Nine Riders cross the Sarn Ford and scatter the Rangers' patrols. An enemy enters the Shire for whom its people are in no way prepared.

events.title: Frodo leaves Bag End
events.summary: Frodo sets out with Sam and Pippin. That same evening the first Black Rider passes through Hobbiton.

events.title: The Old Forest and the Barrow-downs
events.summary: The hobbits pass through the Old Forest, meet Tom Bombadil and escape from the Barrow-downs. From there they also carry away their first weapons — daggers from the barrow of the princes of Cardolan.

events.title: Bree and the meeting with Strider
events.summary: The hobbits come to Bree and at the inn of The Prancing Pony they meet Aragorn, whom the locals call Strider.

events.title: The fight on Weathertop
events.summary: The Nazgûl attack the camp below Amon Sûl. Frodo is wounded by a Morgul-blade — a wound from which he never fully recovers.

events.title: The Ford of Bruinen
events.summary: Frodo crosses the ford on the border of Rivendell. The Nazgûl are swept away by the flood that Elrond commands.

events.title: The Council of Elrond
events.summary: In Rivendell a council of representatives of Elves, Men and Dwarves is held. It is decided that the Ring can neither be used nor hidden and must be destroyed in Orodruin. The Fellowship of the Ring is formed.

events.title: The Fellowship leaves Rivendell
events.summary: Nine companions set out southward. Against the nine Nazgûl stand nine walkers — an elf, a dwarf, two men, four hobbits and a wizard.

years.label: The year 3019
years.intro: The war itself lasts barely three months. The main battles are fought between 3 and 25 March.

events.title: Caradhras
events.summary: The Fellowship tries in vain to cross the pass below Caradhras and turns to Moria.

events.title: The Bridge of Khazad-dûm
events.summary: Gandalf falls into the deeps fighting the Balrog. Without him the Fellowship escapes by the East-gate into Azanulbizar.

events.title: Lothlórien
events.summary: The Fellowship comes to the Golden Wood. Galadriel and Celeborn receive them, give them gifts and let them rest.

events.title: The departure from Lothlórien
events.summary: The Fellowship sails down the Anduin in boats. From that moment Boromir's pressing for the road to Minas Tirith grows ever stronger.

events.title: Parth Galen and the breaking of the Fellowship
events.summary: The Fellowship passes the Argonath and lands at Parth Galen. Boromir tries to take the Ring, then falls defending the hobbits. Merry and Pippin are carried off, Frodo and Sam go on alone towards Mordor.

events.title: The pursuit of the orcs
events.summary: Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli track the orc band across the plains of Rohan. The Rohirrim under Éomer destroy the band near Fangorn, but Merry and Pippin escape into the forest and meet the Ents.

events.title: Gandalf the White
events.summary: Aragorn and his two companions meet Gandalf in Fangorn; he has returned with greater power and a new task.

events.title: Théoden freed
events.summary: Gandalf frees Théoden from Gríma's influence. Rohan openly prepares for war and Éomer is restored to command.

events.title: Helm's Deep and Isengard
events.summary: Saruman's army attacks the Hornburg and is thrown back by the coming of the huorns and the riders. At the same time the Ents flood Isengard and destroy Saruman's industrial base.

events.title: The parley at Orthanc
events.summary: Théoden, Gandalf and their allies come to Orthanc. Saruman refuses a last offer of mercy; Gandalf breaks his power and Pippin gains the palantír.

events.title: Faramir in Ithilien
events.summary: Faramir meets Frodo and Sam, understands what they are carrying and lets them go on. He decides exactly the opposite way to his brother.

events.title: Gandalf and Pippin in Minas Tirith
events.summary: Gandalf brings Pippin to Minas Tirith. Denethor has been watching the enemy through the palantír for weeks and holds the war to be lost.

events.title: The great signal and the Dawnless Day
events.summary: Sauron sends out the signal to attack from Mordor and the shadow out of Mordor covers the sky. The Grey Company comes to Aragorn and he sets out on the Paths of the Dead.

events.title: Cirith Ungol
events.summary: Frodo is attacked by Shelob and taken prisoner by the orcs of Cirith Ungol. Sam rescues him and the two enter Mordor in captured orc-gear.

events.title: The siege of Minas Tirith
events.summary: The Pelennor is flooded with Sauron's armies and the city is cut off. Faramir is wounded, the walls are bombarded and the Rammas Echor falls.

events.title: The Battle of the Pelennor Fields
events.summary: Théoden falls, Éowyn and Merry slay the Witch-king and Aragorn arrives with reinforcements from southern Gondor. On the same day Denethor dies and Saruman loses his influence for ever.

events.title: The decision of the Captains of the West
events.summary: The captains resolve to march to the Black Gate in order to draw Sauron's attention away from the Ring-bearers. It is a deliberate sacrifice, not a hope of military victory. On the same day the battle of Dale begins.

events.title: The host of the West leaves Minas Tirith
events.summary: Not quite seven thousand men ride out to the Morannon — a fraction of what Mordor has at its disposal.

events.title: The destruction of the One Ring
events.summary: Before the Black Gate the battle of the Morannon is fought. Frodo and Sam reach the Sammath Naur, Gollum seizes the Ring and falls with it into the fire. The One Ring is destroyed, Barad-dûr collapses and Sauron's power is at an end.

events.title: The Field of Cormallen
events.summary: Frodo and Sam awake in Ithilien and are honoured before the whole host.

events.title: The crowning of Aragorn
events.summary: Aragorn is crowned as King Elessar Telcontar. The South-kingdom is restored, and with it the claim to Arnor.

events.title: A wedding and funerals
events.summary: Aragorn and Arwen are married at Midsummer. Théoden is buried at Edoras and Éomer becomes King of Rohan. The companions make their way back north one by one.

events.title: The Scouring of the Shire
events.summary: The hobbits come home and find the Shire in the hands of Saruman's men. The Battle of Bywater is fought, the Shire frees itself by its own strength and Saruman dies at Bag End.

fronts.h2: Parallel fronts — the war was not fought in Gondor alone
fronts.intro: The War of the Ring was not only Frodo's journey and the battle for Minas Tirith. In those same days there was fighting in the Elven lands and in the north-east, and the outcome of those battles decided how many forces Sauron could send south.

items.name: Lothlórien
items.desc: Dol Guldur launches three assaults on the Golden Wood. The land of Galadriel and Celeborn withstands them through the power of the Ring Nenya, and after Sauron's fall the host of Lórien destroys Dol Guldur itself and throws down its walls.

items.name: Mirkwood
items.desc: Thranduil's Woodland Realm is attacked out of Dol Guldur. After hard fighting the elves hold their land, and after the war Thranduil and Celeborn meet in the forest; the wood is cleansed and renamed.

items.name: Dale and Erebor
items.desc: Sauron's armies out of the East attack Dale. King Brand and the dwarf-king Dáin II Ironfoot fall before the gate of Erebor. Men and dwarves then hold out inside the mountain until the news of Sauron's defeat spreads and the siege is broken.

items.name: Eriador and the Shire
items.desc: Sauron's main army never strikes the north-west and the Rangers ride south to Aragorn. Saruman's men make use of the emptiness they leave behind and take economic and political control of the Shire. The hobbits free themselves by their own strength only after the war in the south is over.

h_fourth: What changes after Sauron’s fall — the Fourth Age

fourth.intro: The Third Age does not end the moment Sauron falls. Two more years pass between the destruction of the Ring and the end of the age, and the beginning of the Fourth Age is moreover reckoned in two different ways.

events.date_note: Gondor and the hobbits reckon the beginning of the Fourth Age differently — see the note below the timeline.
events.title: The Gondorian reckoning
events.summary: In the Gondorian reckoning the Fourth Age begins on the second anniversary of Sauron's fall. The new age therefore begins on the day of victory, not with the departure of the elves.

events.title: The sailing from the Grey Havens
events.summary: From Mithlond sail Elrond, Galadriel, Gandalf, Bilbo and Frodo. The Three Elven Rings leave Middle-earth, and by the hobbit reckoning the Third Age ends here.

events.title: The age of the rule of Men
events.summary: Aragorn rules the Reunited Kingdom of Arnor and Gondor, Éomer rules Rohan. Dwarves and elves still found new settlements for a while — Gimli in the Glittering Caves, dwarves restoring part of Moria — but the chief power passes to Men.

fourth.note_title: Editorial note on the two calendars
fourth.note_text: The beginning of the Fourth Age can be counted in different ways depending on the calendar used: the Gondorian reckoning places it at 25 March 3021, the hobbit one at the departure of the Ring-bearers on 29 September of the same year. This is neither a mistake nor an inaccuracy in the book, but two different traditions. On this page we give both.

fourth_p1_pre: After the destruction of the One Ring begins the
fourth_p1_post: — the age of Men. Aragorn is crowned as Elessar; the united kingdom of Gondor and Arnor is restored. Rohan and Gondor remain faithful allies.
fourth_p2: Sauron’s direct power falls. Orc bands in the mountains and in Mordor disintegrate — without a central lord they devour each other, vanish into the rocks or eventually attack only in smaller, fragmented raids. Harad and the Easterlings make truce and trade treaties with Gondor.
fourth_p3: For the elves the Fourth Age is a time of departure. The three elven rings lose their power; Galadriel, Elrond, Gildor and many others sail from the Grey Havens. Lothlórien begins slowly to fade, Rivendell loses the power of the Three. The dwarves at Erebor and the Iron Hills prosper, but Khazad-dûm remains lost.

alert_pp_s1: the last years of the Third Age

game.h2: Game timeline of this year's event
game.intro: Book chronology and game chronology should not be mixed in a single list without marking. Everything above this block comes from Tolkien's texts. Everything in this block is our own decision for the game.
game.statement: The 2026 event starts from the world at the end of the Third Age, but it is not a literal reconstruction of the War of the Ring. It is an alternative game branch inspired by the end of the Third Age — some groups will meet on the battlefield at a moment when, according to the books, they could not have met, and part of the events may turn out differently than in the book.
